authorization.requires: Fresh explicit owner authorization for the named arms, compute budget and synthetic-dataset generation before any run; the 2.00 CU V2 campaign ledger is not reused or reset.

arms.ZERO_SHOT_UNCONSTRAINED: Pinned SmolLM3, V3 prompt and native xml_tools, greedy generation under the profile decoding bounds. Measures syntax plus intent.
arms.ZERO_SHOT_CONSTRAINED: Pinned SmolLM3, same prompt, scripts/a02_v3_constrained.py grammar walk. Syntax control: removes format failure, isolates choice quality.
arms.ADAPTED_UNCONSTRAINED: Supervised-adapted candidate, native generation as in the first arm.
arms.ADAPTED_CONSTRAINED: Supervised-adapted candidate under the same grammar walk.
arms.STRONGER_MODEL_ZERO_SHOT: Optional; only if the rule escalates. Requires a separate preregistration naming the model.

adaptation.method: LoRA supervised fine-tuning on target_text tokens only (loss masked on prompt tokens); prompt rendered with the V3 action prompt and xml_tools exactly as at evaluation
adaptation.model_selection: No checkpoint selection on held-out data; the final checkpoint after the fixed schedule is evaluated once.

data.rights: Fully synthetic, generated by repository code; no external, empirical, RES-407 protected or RES-424 formal data.

heldout_evaluation.role: Sole decision input; never trained on or used for selection.

exposed_development_cases.role: DEVELOPMENT_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY: reported per arm on every axis, including executor and final grounding; never training data, never held-out evidence, never a decision input.

generated_semantics.role: Closed-vocabulary adjudication of the complete generator phrasing, written from template text and not from family labels. Every training and held-out gold action is independently derived from it; load_protocol refuses any generator whose gold differs for any example, and no example is skipped.

gold_independence.limit: The adjudication is project-authored. It checks the internal consistency of the synthetic task, not that this phrasing resembles how real staff ask.

calibration.role: Cache qualification only. Training-split examples that are never evaluated and are disjoint from every held-out and exposed request. They are the only requests the model sees before cache correctness is established.

metrics.primary: Exact V3 intent on the held-out set (strict parse and normalized equality with spec gold).
secondary: operation selection where gold names one
deferred: raw final grounding on exposed cases: the zero-shot worker collects actions only; a final-answer stage needs its own prompt and amendment before any final is scored

zero_shot_sufficient.lower_bound_basis: Template-cluster-aware 95% lower confidence bound (the smaller of the item-level and template-clustered percentile bounds, 10000 resamples) on the zero-shot constrained arm's overall exact rate AND its critical-family exact rate.
zero_shot_sufficient.rule: Adopt only if both point thresholds and both lower bounds reach 0.90. If both point thresholds pass but a lower bound does not, the result is INCONCLUSIVE_INSUFFICIENT_INDEPENDENT_EVIDENCE: not adoption, and not eligibility to study adaptation. If a point threshold fails on a complete, valid evaluation, the result is ADAPTATION_STUDY_ELIGIBLE_NOT_AUTHORIZED.
zero_shot_sufficient.thresholds_frozen: No threshold may be changed after any V3 model observation.

statistics.method: Paired percentile bootstrap at item level and with whole templates resampled as clusters. For the adaptation-benefit gain checks the smaller lower bound governs.
statistics.cluster_unit: generator template_id; examples sharing a template are correlated
statistics.sufficiency_basis: Adoption needs the point estimate and the template-cluster-aware 95% lower bound to reach 0.90 on both the overall and the critical-family exact rate. The report also gives cluster counts, effective cluster size, per-family performance with Wilson intervals, leave-one-template-out sensitivity and the limitations of the bounds.

decision_rule.stage_1_meaning: Stage 1 observes only the zero-shot arms. A point failure on a complete, valid evaluation makes proposing an adaptation study eligible, subject to separate authorization. It is not evidence that adaptation would help and it authorizes no training. An inconclusive result is neither.

adaptation_benefit.requires: Observed ADAPTED_CONSTRAINED records bound to the same held-out examples.

decision_rule.evidence_binding: scripts/a02_v3_decision.py::bind_arm: exact preregistered example ids in order; no duplicates, gaps or extras; family, request hash, arm, decoder, model revision, profile and protocol hashes; raw-output hash; correctness recomputed from raw output
reported_not_credited: decoder_condition_exact_gap (includes constrained-search and selection effects, not syntax alone)
reported_every_decision: cluster_design and critical_cluster_design (items, template clusters, effective clusters)
exact_lower_bounds and critical_exact_lower_bounds per zero-shot arm

compute_estimate.input_sources: Preflight (pinned tokenizer, V3 profile): max prompt 1,508 tokens, max gold-path cached fed tokens 1,932, max scorer calls 69, action cap 128. Session 004 T4 FP16: max steady first-token latency 0.41 s, min steady decode 23.05 tokens/s, 77.7 s pre-generation overhead plus a 35.6 s model load rounded to 113 s.
compute_estimate.consequence: Both zero-shot arms need about 46 minutes (2,735.7 s) of T4 time: more than one 900 s session, so any run needs a budget sized for it. Exposed-case diagnostics add 10 examples per arm. The adapted arms add training time, which is not estimated here because no training is authorized.
compute_estimate.scorer: Constrained arms use CachedSequenceLogprob with HFIncrementalBackend. Uncached full re-scoring would need up to 68,703 scored tokens per example instead of 1,932.
compute_estimate.admission: Superseded for admission by the worst-case session plan (scripts/a02_v3_execution.py::build_plan), which uses bounds looser than every session-004 observation and adds per-session prepare, inference overhead and cache-qualification costs.

in_run_qualification: Before any arm result counts: score every option on the three calibration examples (data.calibration; not held-out) with both the cached and the uncached reference binding; abort the run if any option differs by more than 1e-3 nats or the chosen action differs. The qualification record binds the model id and revision.
Verify the pinned model and tokenizer revisions and file hashes, and that rendered prompts reproduce the CPU preflight hashes.
Record raw generations, token ids and per-option scores for every example; score on CPU with scripts/a02_v3_score.py and scripts/a02_v3_decision.py only.

On every resume the worker verifies that every committed record carries the preregistered model id and revision, contract profile hash and protocol hash, and that the work list equals execution.work_list; any drift fails closed before a new item is evaluated. The controller applies the same identity check to downloaded evidence before adopting it.

amendments.reason: Independent review #5824688227 P0 on objective/question precedence.

amendments.change: Arm records are bound to exact preregistered example identity, family, request hash and model, profile and protocol provenance, with correctness recomputed from raw output. The syntax-gap label is replaced by a strict-parse gap and a decoder-condition gap, neither credited. Template-clustered bootstrap is added and governs when more conservative, with per-family Wilson intervals. Stage 1 concludes only adoption or eligibility for an adaptation experiment; benefit needs observed adapted records.
amendments.reason: Independent review #5824688227 P0 evidence integrity, P1 statistics and staged decision.

amendments.change: Execution is bound to the resumable worker, session controller and remote bootstrap; admission uses the worst-case session plan rather than the point estimate. Exposed-case diagnostics in the zero-shot run are action-level only; raw final grounding is deferred, not claimed.
amendments.reason: Independent review #5824688227 P0 runtime readiness; no final-answer stage exists for V3.

amendments.change: Generated gold is independently derived for all 2,800 training and 280 held-out examples from a pinned closed-vocabulary adjudication. Cache qualification moves from held-out examples to training-split calibration examples. Committed and downloaded records are identity-checked, the ordered work list is pinned, and the plan is priced from the whole workload (scorer-call bound 73). Per-session owner authorizations become one finite campaign allowance with stop-on-first-anomaly. Cluster design and single-arm lower bounds are reported; the sufficiency rule is unchanged.
amendments.reason: Closes the findings of the RES-541 continuation gates 3 and 4: the generator was its own gold oracle, qualification read protected requests, and the plan understated the held-out workload.

amendments.change: Adoption now also requires the template-cluster-aware 95% lower bound to reach 0.90 on both overall and critical-family exact rate. Point thresholds stay at 0.90. A point pass with an insufficient bound returns INCONCLUSIVE_INSUFFICIENT_INDEPENDENT_EVIDENCE. A point failure returns ADAPTATION_STUDY_ELIGIBLE_NOT_AUTHORIZED (renamed from ELIGIBLE_FOR_ADAPTATION_EXPERIMENT). Leave-one-template-out sensitivity, critical-family cluster design and confidence-bound limitations are reported.
amendments.reason: The held-out set has 15 template clusters (about 8.1 effective), so a point estimate at the threshold carries little independent evidence. Owner decision on RES-541 to amend the rule prospectively.

supersedes.stage_1_meaning: Stage 1 observes only the zero-shot arms. Failing the sufficiency rule makes an adaptation experiment eligible for separate authorization; it is not evidence that adaptation would help.
supersedes.statistics.sufficiency_basis: Stage 1 sufficiency compares point estimates with the thresholds. Each zero-shot arm's item-level and template-clustered lower bounds on its exact rate, the cluster design and the per-family Wilson intervals are reported with the decision and do not change it.
supersedes.sufficiency_caution: With about 8 effective template clusters a point estimate at the 0.90 threshold can have a clustered lower bound far below it. Adopting the repaired contract is an engineering decision on same-generator development evidence, not a finding that the model is sufficient.
supersedes.original_text: Zero-shot constrained exact >= 0.90 and critical-family exact >= 0.90 on point estimates adopted the repaired contract; otherwise an adaptation experiment became eligible.

amendments.preserved: The original preregistration is retained verbatim in this record and in Git history (commit bbbe820).

claim_ceiling: Results bound SmolLM3 behaviour on one synthetic development generator whose train and held-out splits share its 14 intent families. They are not evidence of scientific generalization, real-request safety, or PSE readiness. The ten exposed cases are diagnostics. Summed log-probability selection can favour short options such as NONE or an empty list, so the constrained arm's errors are decoder-and-model choices, not proof of understanding or inability. Generated gold agrees with a project-authored closed-vocabulary adjudication of the generator's own phrasing, which checks internal consistency of the synthetic task and not real-request phrasing. The held-out set has 15 template clusters (about 8 effective), so adoption also requires the cluster-aware lower bound to reach 0.90 and an insufficient bound is reported as inconclusive. CPU qualification used a tiny random model, and the Colab GPU path is unverified.

execution.worker: scripts/a02_v3_worker.py (hash-chained resumable checkpoint, deadline-bounded, cache qualification on calibration examples first)
execution.controller: scripts/a02_v3_execution.py (worst-case session plan priced from the whole workload, one finite campaign allowance, stop-on-first-anomaly campaign with no retry, V3-only ledger, exact-target teardown)

work_list.order: qualification, then every held-out example with both zero-shot arms in order, then the ten exposed cases with both arms

bound_identities.model: candidate_model (id and revision), verified in every committed record and in the backend

campaign_allowance.rule: One expiring owner grant bound to the exact plan hash replaces per-session authorizations. It can only tighten the plan's session count and compute-unit caps. Each session still rechecks the ledger, caps, live balance and usage attribution. The campaign stops at the first anomaly and never retries a session; a later invocation is a deliberate new action.

scorer_call_bound.basis: maximum over held-out, calibration and exposed requests

session_budget.feasibility: All 581 items pack into nine sessions under worst-case costs with little slack; real runs are expected to need fewer. The corrected scorer-call bound (73, from the held-out set rather than the 69 of the ten exposed cases) is what makes this the true worst case.

qualification_limits: CPU qualification used a tiny randomly initialised SmolLM3ForCausalLM in float32, not the pinned weights. It shows the cache logic is correct on a real Transformers model, not that FP16 CUDA on a T4 stays within 1e-3 nats.
The cache is qualified once, in session 1, on that session's runtime. Later sessions run on fresh VMs and are not re-qualified, because a per-session re-qualification does not fit nine sessions.
If the in-run qualification fails, no arm result counts and that session's compute units are spent.
Timing and cost are worst-case bounds derived from session 004, not from any V3 observation. The Colab GPU path is unverified.
